newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Global zinc smelting near capacity - Pasminco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Global zinc smelting near capacity - Pasminco.

text.p: The world's zinc smelting industry is forecast to continue operating at about 90 percent of full capacity, an official of Pasminco Ltd, the world's biggest zinc producer, said in a paper to be delivered on Wednesday at a commodities conference here.

Growth in potential mine output of zinc is expected to grow 24 percent by the year 2000 to seven million tonnes, which will exceed growth in smelting, John Winckel, Pasminco's metals general manager, said in the paper.
Winckel forecast that inventories of zinc at the London Metal Exchange and in the hands of producers would continue to decrease in the short term, which should shore up prices.
But this would probably encourage more smelters to open, making the higher prices unsustainable, he added.

Growth in demand for zinc in Europe and North America would be at rates of less than one percent through the end of the decade while Asia should record annual growth of around 3.7 percent, Winckel said.
"Asia will drive world zinc consumption growth over the next 10 years," Winckel said.
Annual growth in consumption of zinc in China was likely to be closer to five percent, he added.
